chapter_title: [Concerning the Interpretation of] all [the] Fathers of [Light], who are distinguished from one another.
chapter_note: This chapter is a catechetical-style catalogue of principal Light divinities. Most paragraphs are written in a repetitive “The beginning of X is Y” application register that maps cosmic beings onto worldly virtues/roles (grace, prayer, hunters, builders, etc.), suggesting a later didactic recasting of an older list. The recoverable core is the underlying enumeration of named Fathers of Light and a few brief cosmological functions (notably the Living Spirit and his five sons; the Light Mind as awakener/gatherer). The opening speech-attribution is frame, and the closing beatitudes are exhortational/pastoral.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic dialogue attribution and audience-address (“Once again the enlightener speaks… my beloved ones”) and the catechetical/application framing (“[the beginn]ing of every good grace… since… graces…”), which maps the Father onto devotional ‘grace’ language rather than expounding cosmic architecture.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula + direct address mark late compilation voice; only the divine title itself plausibly preserves older catalog material.

paragraphs.core_text: the Mother of [L]ife, the first Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause “The beginning of each blessing and every prayer is…”, which maps the cosmic figure onto prayer/blessing practice (cosmos→world).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying divine name is cosmological; the ‘beginning of prayer/blessing’ rubric reads like later instructional recasting. ‘Holy Spirit’ here functions as a Manichaean divine title rather than an explicit NT citation.

paragraphs.core_text: the T[h/i]rd Am[bassad]or, the king of the glorious realm that lies in this [wo]rld, [ ... ] of the King of the lights.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause “Also, [the] beginning [of] every good [co]unsel is…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The remaining material is a straight cosmological identification (named being + realm/kingly function), consistent with an older catalogue; the ‘good counsel’ mapping is didactic.

paragraphs.core_text: the Beloved of the Lights, who is honour[ed.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause “The beginning of [ ... and] each [hono]ur (?) is…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying divine title likely comes from an older list; the paragraph’s rubric (‘beginning of honour’) is application-style rather than mechanistic cosmology.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause “The beginning of a]ll [the trappers] and hunters is…”, which maps the cosmic being to a worldly occupation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “First Man” is a stable Persian-Manichaean cosmological name; ‘hunters/trappers’ reads like later pedagogical analogy.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.44⟩
[the] Living [Spirit], the Father of Life, who has distribu[ted about] his five sons from place to place.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the rubric fragment “… of] all fighters is …”, which maps the Living Spirit to ‘fighters’; retained the cosmological function describing distribution of the five sons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The five-sons distribution is characteristic core system-language (structural, cosmological, impersonal). The ‘fighters’ linkage is a didactic overlay on that content.

paragraphs.core_text: the Great Builder, who is glorious.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause “The beginning of all the archit[e]cts and builders is…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic title preserved, but the occupational mapping (‘architects/builders’) suggests later instructional framing rather than the oldest internal cosmic mapping.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause “Also, the first of all the porters of the gr[e]a[t]ness is…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “Pillar of Glory” is a core cosmological entity; the ‘porters of greatness’ rubric reads like a pedagogical metaphor applied to a known figure.

paragraphs.core_text: [is Jesus the Splendour]; or the one who delivers, as he frees whoever belongs [ ... ] from his words.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the rubric “The beginning of [all] the deliverers …”, retaining the identification and salvific function statement.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “Jesus the Splendour” here functions as a named Manichaean cosmic deliverer (core-compatible) rather than a Gospel citation; the ‘deliverers’ category is an application-style label.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the catechetical/application clause “The beginning of every wisdom of truth is…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying divine name is part of the standard Light hierarchy; the ‘wisdom of truth’ rubric reads like later catechesis.

paragraphs.core_text: the Light Mind; who is the awakene[r of they] who sleep, the gatherer in of the ones who are sc[att]ered.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the rubric “The beginning of] all [the great]est honoured ones [ ... ] is…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The functional pair ‘awakener’/‘gatherer-in’ is close to core expository language describing cosmic operations; the ‘honoured ones’ category is a didactic framing.
Beatitude/exhortation addressed to the hearer (“Blessed is he… lodge… fasten… in his heart”)—application voice rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Closing beatitude promising inheritance of eternal life; exhortational conclusion to the catalogue rather than core system-description.
